title: Archive the Payment Run
scenario: It is 3:05 PM. The run is delivered, the vendor is notified, the desk is quiet. One step remains, and it is the one that makes tomorrow possible: archive today's run. Archiving is not just filing - it seeds the payment history so tomorrow's duplicate check knows INV-58831 was already paid. Close the loop.
input: Today's run: INV-58831 (V-1042, 1220.00), paid day-1. Archiving stores the run for audit retention AND appends its invoices to the payment history using the identity key (vendor id + invoice number + total). Tomorrow's duplicate check reads that history - so today's output becomes tomorrow's guardrail.
instructions: Read the archive as both an audit record and the seed for tomorrow's duplicate baseline.
Answer the four questions about retention and the temporal loop.
Validate to mint the payment-archive record.

questions.prompt: Besides audit retention, what does archiving the run do?

options.text: Nothing else - it just files the run
It appends the run's invoices to the payment history

questions.explain: The archive seeds the payment history with today's payments. That is what makes the duplicate check work tomorrow - it can only catch a repeat if today's payment is recorded.

questions.prompt: Which workflow step reads what this archive seeds?

options.text: Tomorrow's Duplicate Check, via the Payment History

questions.explain: Follow the map's temporal loop: archive seeds payment history, and payment history feeds the duplicate check on the next run. Today's output is tomorrow's reference.

questions.prompt: What identity is stored so a future duplicate can be caught?

options.text: Vendor id + invoice number + invoice total

questions.explain: The same identity key the duplicate check uses is what the archive writes, so tomorrow a re-submitted INV-58831 for V-1042 at 1220.00 is recognized as already paid.

questions.prompt: Why does the archive point back to a reference node instead of forward to a new step?

options.text: It is a mistake in the map
The workflow is a daily cycle - its output feeds the next day's inputs
Archives always point backward for no reason

questions.explain: The desk runs every day. The archive does not end the story - it feeds payment history, which is a reference for the next run. That backward edge is the loop that makes the workflow repeatable.

sections.title: Archiving is not just filing
sections.body: The archive keeps the run for audit, yes - but it also appends today's invoices to the payment history. That second job is what makes the desk repeatable, not just complete.

sections.title: The temporal loop
sections.body: On the map, this archive points back to a reference node, not forward. The workflow is a daily cycle: today's output becomes an input to tomorrow's run. That backward edge is the loop.

sections.title: Same identity, next day
sections.body: The archive stores each payment by vendor id + invoice number + total - the exact key the duplicate check uses. So a re-submitted INV-58831 tomorrow is caught as already paid.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A payment-archive record: retained for audit, seeding the payment history. It is the final artifact - and the one that lets the whole desk run clean again tomorrow.

points: You answered the four questions: what archiving does beyond retention, who reads it next, the identity stored, and why the loop points backward.
The archive seeds the payment history with today's payments, so tomorrow's duplicate check can catch a repeat.
It stores each payment by vendor id + invoice number + total - the same key the duplicate check reads.
